# Numerical semigroups generated by powers

7 results, 7 stated but not proved, quoted from [Deicyde/atlas-lean](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean) at commit [a3690dd2](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/tree/a3690dd2ad41e1ad4d871b062779ed7b0452800d); [its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-powers/index.html).

## Minimal generators of the tail semigroups of an increasing sequence

Let
$x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers. For $m \ge 1$
let $S_m$ be the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $x_m, x_{m+1}, \ldots$, and let
$\beta(S_m)$ be its set of minimal generators, the nonzero elements of $S_m$ that are not the sum
of two nonzero elements of $S_m$. For $k \ge 1$ let $r_k$ be the least $m \ge 1$ with
$x_k \in \beta(S_m)$. Then for all integers $k, n \ge 1$, $x_k \in \beta(S_n)$ if and only if
$r_k \le n \le k$; and the embedding dimension $e(S_n) = |\beta(S_n)|$ equals the number of
integers $j \ge 1$ with $r_j \le n \le j$.

The paper's standing assumption $\gcd(x_n, x_{n+1}, \ldots) = 1$ is not needed and is dropped.

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Lemma 1.

[Its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-powers/index.html#mem-minimal-generators-iff-first-appeara).

## Embedding dimension bound from linear growth of first appearances

Let
$x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers. For $m \ge 1$
let $S_m$ be the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $x_m, x_{m+1}, \ldots$; call a
nonzero element of $S_m$ that is not the sum of two nonzero elements of $S_m$ a minimal generator
of $S_m$, and let the embedding dimension $e(S_m)$ be the number of minimal generators of $S_m$.
For $k \ge 1$ let $r_k$ be the least $m \ge 1$ such that $x_k$ is a minimal generator of $S_m$.
If $\alpha > 0$ is a real number with $r_k \ge \alpha k$ for all $k \ge 1$, then
$e(S_n) \le \lfloor n / \alpha \rfloor - n + 1$ for all $n \ge 1$.

The paper's standing assumption $\gcd(x_n, x_{n+1}, \ldots) = 1$ is not needed and is dropped.

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Proposition 1.

Stated but not proved: `MetaMathlibExt.embeddingDimension_le_of_firstAppearance_ge` is written with `theorem_wanted` in [WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean, line 64](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/blob/a3690dd2ad41e1ad4d871b062779ed7b0452800d/WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean#L64). ## Four squares with large nonzero parts

There is a real constant $C > 0$ such that every
positive integer $n$ can be written as $n = a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2 + a_4^2$ with integers
$a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4$, each of which is either $0$ or at least $\sqrt{n} / C$.

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Lemma 2, quoting A. Moscariello.

Stated but not proved: `MetaMathlibExt.exists_four_squares_large_parts` is written with `theorem_wanted` in [WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean, line 81](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/blob/a3690dd2ad41e1ad4d871b062779ed7b0452800d/WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean#L81). [Its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-powers/index.html#exists-four-squares-large-parts).

## Dutch–Rickett conductor inequality for a union of generating sets

For a set $X$ of
natural numbers, let $\tau(X)$ be the conductor of the additive submonoid $\langle X \rangle$ of
$\mathbb{N}$ generated by $X$, the least natural number $c$ such that every $j \ge c$ lies in
$\langle X \rangle$. Let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty sets of natural numbers such that $1$ is the only
natural number dividing every element of $A \cup B$, let $t$ be a natural number dividing every
element of $A$, and let $C = \{a / t : a \in A\}$ (with $a / 0 = 0$). Then

$$\tau(A \cup B) \le t \, \tau(C \cup B) + \tau(B \cup \{t\}).$$

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Lemma 3, quoting K. Dutch and C. Rickett.

Stated but not proved: `MetaMathlibExt.conductor_union_le` is written with `theorem_wanted` in [WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean, line 92](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/blob/a3690dd2ad41e1ad4d871b062779ed7b0452800d/WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean#L92). [Its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-powers/index.html#conductor-union-le).

## Dutch–Rickett conductor recursion for semigroups of $k$-th powers

Fix an integer
$k \ge 1$. For $m \ge 1$ let $S_m$ be the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by
$m^k, (m+1)^k, (m+2)^k, \ldots$, and let $\tau(S_m)$ be its conductor, the least natural number
$c$ such that every $j \ge c$ lies in $S_m$. Then for every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\tau(S_n) \le 2^k \, \tau(S_{\lceil n/2 \rceil}) + (2^k - 1)(2n)^k.$$

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Proposition 2, inequality (3), quoting K. Dutch and C. Rickett.

## Semigroups of squares have embedding dimension $O(n)$

For $n \ge 1$ let $S_n$ be the
additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $n^2, (n+1)^2, (n+2)^2, \ldots$, and let $e(S_n)$
be its embedding dimension, the number of nonzero elements of $S_n$ that are not the sum of two
nonzero elements of $S_n$. There is a natural number $C$ with $e(S_n) \le C n$ for all $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Theorem 1.

Stated but not proved: `MetaMathlibExt.embeddingDimension_squares_isBigO` is written with `theorem_wanted` in [WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean, line 116](https://github.com/Deicyde/atlas-lean/blob/a3690dd2ad41e1ad4d871b062779ed7b0452800d/WantedExt/NumberTheory/NumericalSemigroupsKthPowersWanted.lean#L116). [Its page on the ATLAS site](https://deicyde.github.io/atlas-lean/roadmap/NumberTheory/numerical-semigroups/numerical-semigroups-generated-by-powers/index.html#embedding-dimension-squares-is-big-o).

## Frobenius numbers of semigroups of $k$-th powers are $O(n^{k+\varepsilon})$

Let $k \ge 2$
be an integer and $\varepsilon > 0$ a real number. For $n \ge 1$ let $S_n$ be the additive
submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $n^k, (n+1)^k, (n+2)^k, \ldots$. Then there is a real
constant $K$ such that for every $n \ge 1$, if $S_n$ has a Frobenius number $F$ (the largest
natural number not in $S_n$), then $F \le K n^{k + \varepsilon}$.

Since $S_1 = \mathbb{N}$ has no Frobenius number, the case $n = 1$ is vacuous.

## Sources

- Fabián Arias, Jerson Borja and Jaider Terán, *A Note on Numerical Semigroups Generated by k-th Powers*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A11, Theorem 2.
